source.text: וְדָוִ֗ד עָבַ֤ר מְעַט֙ מֵֽהָרֹ֔אשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר מְפִי־בֹ֖שֶׁת לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וְצֶ֨מֶד חֲמֹרִ֜ים חֲבֻשִׁ֗ים וַעֲלֵיהֶם֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּמֵאָ֧ה צִמּוּקִ֛ים וּמֵ֥אָה קַ֖יִץ וְנֵ֥בֶל יָֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: And David passed a little from the top, and look, Ziba, [the] attendant of Mephibosheth, to meet him, and a pair of donkeys saddled, and on them 200 bread and 100 raisin clusters and 100 summer fruit and a skin of wine.

en.L: And David had passed a little beyond the summit, and look, Ziba the attendant of Mephibosheth [was there] to meet him, with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them 200 [loaves of] bread and 100 clusters of raisins and 100 [portions of] summer fruit and a skin of wine.
en.B: David had gone a little way past the top of the hill when Ziba, Mephibosheth's attendant, met him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 portions of summer fruit and a skin of wine.
en.R: David had gone just a short way past the top of the Mount of Olives when Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, came to meet him. Ziba had two donkeys with saddles on them. They carried 200 loaves of bread, 100 bunches of raisins, 100 portions of ripe summer fruit, and a skin bag full of wine.

es.L: Y David había pasado un poco más allá de la cumbre, y he aquí, Siba, el servidor de Mefiboset, [salió] a su encuentro con un par de asnos aparejados, y sobre ellos doscientos [panes de] pan, cien racimos de pasas, cien [porciones de] fruta de verano y un odre de vino.
es.B: David había pasado un poco más allá de la cumbre cuando Siba, el servidor de Mefiboset, salió a su encuentro. Traía un par de asnos aparejados, cargados con doscientos panes, cien racimos de pasas, cien porciones de fruta de verano y un odre de vino.
es.R: David había caminado un poco más allá de la cima del monte de los Olivos cuando Siba, el siervo de Mefiboset, salió a su encuentro. Siba traía dos asnos con sus monturas. Venían cargados con doscientos panes, cien racimos de pasas, cien porciones de fruta madura del verano y un odre lleno de vino.

fr.L: Et David avait passé un peu au-delà du sommet, et voici, Tsiba, le serviteur de Mephibosheth, [vint] à sa rencontre, avec une paire d’ânes sellés, et sur eux deux cents [pains], cent grappes de raisins secs, cent [portions de] fruits d’été et une outre de vin.
fr.B: David avait à peine dépassé le sommet quand Tsiba, l’intendant de Mephibosheth, vint à sa rencontre. Il avait deux ânes sellés, chargés de deux cents pains, de cent grappes de raisins secs, de cent portions de fruits d’été et d’une outre de vin.
fr.R: David venait de dépasser le sommet du mont des Oliviers quand Tsiba, le serviteur de Mephibosheth, est venu à sa rencontre. Tsiba avait deux ânes sellés. Ils portaient deux cents pains, cent grappes de raisins secs, cent portions de fruits mûrs de l’été et une outre pleine de vin.

sw.L: Daudi alipokuwa amepita kidogo kutoka kileleni, tazama, Siba mhudumu wa Mefiboshethi [alikuwa huko] kumlaki, akiwa na punda wawili waliotandikwa, na juu yao [mikate] 200 na vishada 100 vya zabibu kavu na [mafungu] 100 ya matunda ya kiangazi na kiriba cha divai.
sw.B: Daudi alipokuwa amepita kidogo kutoka kilele cha kilima, Siba, mhudumu wa Mefiboshethi, akakutana naye. Alikuwa na punda wawili waliotandikwa, wakiwa wamebeba mikate 200, vishada 100 vya zabibu kavu, mafungu 100 ya matunda ya kiangazi na kiriba cha divai.
sw.R: Daudi alipokuwa amekwenda mwendo mfupi tu kupita kilele cha mlima wa Mizeituni, Siba, mtumishi wa Mefiboshethi, akaja kumlaki. Siba alikuwa na punda wawili waliotandikwa. Walibeba mikate 200, vishada 100 vya zabibu kavu, mafungu 100 ya matunda mabivu ya kiangazi, na kiriba kilichojaa divai.

vi.L: Đa-vít vừa đi qua khỏi đỉnh núi một chút, thì kìa, Xíp-ba, quản gia của Mê-phi-bô-sết, [đến] đón vua với một cặp lừa đã thắng yên, trên lưng chở 200 [ổ] bánh, 100 chùm nho khô, 100 [phần] trái cây mùa hạ và một bầu da rượu.
vi.B: Đa-vít vừa qua khỏi đỉnh núi một quãng thì Xíp-ba, quản gia của Mê-phi-bô-sết, đến đón vua. Ông dắt theo một cặp lừa đã thắng yên, chở 200 ổ bánh, 100 chùm nho khô, 100 phần trái cây mùa hạ và một bầu da rượu.
vi.R: Đa-vít vừa đi qua khỏi đỉnh núi Ô-li-ve một đoạn ngắn thì Xíp-ba, đầy tớ của Mê-phi-bô-sết, đến gặp vua. Xíp-ba dắt theo hai con lừa có thắng yên. Lừa chở 200 ổ bánh, 100 chùm nho khô, 100 phần trái cây chín mùa hè và một bầu da đầy rượu.

ko.L: 다윗이 산꼭대기를 조금 지나갔을 때, 보라, 므비보셋의 시종 시바가 안장을 얹은 나귀 두 마리를 끌고 그를 맞으러 [나왔다]. 나귀 위에는 빵 이백 [덩이]와 건포도 백 송이와 여름 과일 백 [개]와 포도주 한 가죽 부대가 [실려] 있었다.
ko.B: 다윗이 산꼭대기를 조금 지났을 때, 므비보셋의 시종 시바가 그를 맞으러 나왔다. 시바는 안장을 얹은 나귀 두 마리를 끌고 왔는데, 나귀에는 빵 이백 덩이와 건포도 백 송이와 여름 과일 백 개와 포도주 한 부대가 실려 있었다.
ko.R: 다윗이 올리브 산 꼭대기를 조금 지나갔을 때, 므비보셋의 종 시바가 다윗을 맞으러 왔다. 시바는 안장을 얹은 나귀 두 마리를 끌고 왔다. 나귀에는 빵 이백 덩이, 건포도 백 송이, 잘 익은 여름 과일 백 개, 그리고 포도주가 가득 든 가죽 부대 하나가 실려 있었다.

decisions.choice: the summit: the top of the Mount of Olives, where God was worshiped
decisions.reason: David left Jerusalem by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping, and met Hushai at the summit, "where God was worshiped" (15:30, 32). He has just passed over it on the road down toward the Jordan.

decisions.choice: attendant: the steward who managed Mephibosheth's estate
decisions.reason: The word often means a young man, but here, as in 9:9, it names the man in charge of a household's affairs. David had made Ziba, with his sons and servants, farm Saul's land for Mephibosheth (9:9-10).

decisions.choice: summer fruit: the late-summer crop, such as figs
decisions.reason: The word means summer and also the fruit gathered at the end of summer (Jeremiah 40:10; Amos 8:1-2). Like the raisins, it was food that travelers could carry and eat at once (1 Samuel 25:18).

decisions.choice: [loaves of] bread; [portions of] summer fruit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts the bread and the fruit without naming a unit. Literal brackets the words English needs; Balanced and Readable say them plainly.

decisions.choice: the top of the Mount of Olives; servant
decisions.reason: Readable names the hill from 15:30 so the reader knows where David is, and calls Ziba Mephibosheth's servant, the plainer word for his place in the household.

decisions.choice: Siba, el servidor de Mefiboset (L, B); el siervo de Mefiboset (R)
decisions.reason: Siba and Mefiboset as the terms note. Ziba is the steward of Saul's house (9:2, 9), so Literal and Balanced say 'servidor', the attendant who serves him, and Readable 'siervo', as the English 'servant'.

decisions.choice: Siba, Mefiboshethi
decisions.reason: The forms of the Samuel terms note; used through this block.

decisions.choice: "Xíp-ba, quản gia của Mê-phi-bô-sết" (L, B); "đầy tớ" (R)
decisions.reason: Names as the Samuel terms note gives them; "quản gia" for the man who managed the estate (meaning decision), Readable the plainer "đầy tớ" as the English "servant".

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־צִיבָ֖א מָה־אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר צִ֠יבָא הַחֲמוֹרִ֨ים לְבֵית־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְכֹּ֗ב וְהַלֶּ֤חֶם וְהַקַּ֨יִץ֙ לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְהַיַּ֕יִן לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת הַיָּעֵ֖ף בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Ziba, what [are] these to you? And said Ziba, the donkeys [are] for [the] household of the king to ride, and the bread and the summer fruit to eat [for] the young men, and the wine to drink [for] the faint [one] in the wilderness.

en.L: And the king said to Ziba, "What [are] these [things] to you?" And Ziba said, "The donkeys [are] for the king's household to ride, and the bread and the summer fruit [are] for the young men to eat, and the wine [is] for whoever is faint in the wilderness to drink."
en.B: The king asked Ziba, "What do you mean by these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on. The bread and the summer fruit are food for the young men, and the wine is for anyone who grows faint in the wilderness."
en.R: The king asked Ziba, "What are these things for?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and the fruit are food for your young men. And the wine is for anyone who becomes weak and tired in the desert."

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Siba: «¿Qué [son] para ti estas [cosas]?». Y Siba dijo: «Los asnos [son] para que monte la casa del rey, y el pan y la fruta de verano [son] para que coman los jóvenes, y el vino [es] para que beba el que se fatigue en el desierto».
es.B: El rey le preguntó a Siba: «¿Qué piensas hacer con esto?». Siba respondió: «Los asnos son para que monte la familia del rey. El pan y la fruta de verano son para que coman los jóvenes, y el vino para el que se desfallezca en el desierto».
es.R: El rey le preguntó a Siba: «¿Para qué es todo esto?». Siba respondió: «Los asnos son para que monte tu familia. El pan y la fruta son para que coman tus jóvenes. Y el vino es para cualquiera que se sienta débil y cansado en el desierto».

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Tsiba : « Que [veux]-tu [faire] de cela ? » Et Tsiba dit : « Les ânes [sont] pour que la maison du roi les monte, et le pain et les fruits d’été pour que les jeunes gens les mangent, et le vin pour que boive celui qui sera épuisé dans le désert. »
fr.B: Le roi demanda à Tsiba : « Que veux-tu faire de tout cela ? » Tsiba répondit : « Les ânes sont pour que la famille du roi puisse les monter. Le pain et les fruits d’été sont pour nourrir les jeunes gens, et le vin pour ceux qui seront à bout de forces dans le désert. »
fr.R: Le roi a demandé à Tsiba : « À quoi servent toutes ces choses ? » Tsiba a répondu : « Les ânes, c’est pour que ta famille puisse les monter. Le pain et les fruits, c’est pour nourrir tes jeunes hommes. Et le vin, c’est pour ceux qui seront faibles et fatigués dans le désert. »

sw.L: Mfalme akamwambia Siba, "Haya [ni ya nini] kwako?" Siba akasema, "Punda [ni] kwa ajili ya watu wa nyumba ya mfalme kupanda, na mikate na matunda ya kiangazi [ni] kwa ajili ya vijana kula, na divai [ni] kwa ajili ya yeyote atakayezimia nyikani kunywa."
sw.B: Mfalme akamwuliza Siba, "Unakusudia nini kwa vitu hivi?" Siba akajibu, "Punda ni kwa ajili ya watu wa nyumbani mwa mfalme kupanda. Mikate na matunda ya kiangazi ni chakula cha vijana, na divai ni kwa ajili ya yeyote atakayechoka sana nyikani."
sw.R: Mfalme akamwuliza Siba, "Vitu hivi ni vya nini?" Siba akajibu, "Punda ni kwa ajili ya jamaa yako kupanda. Mikate na matunda ni chakula cha vijana wako. Na divai ni kwa ajili ya yeyote atakayedhoofika na kuchoka huko jangwani."

vi.L: Vua nói với Xíp-ba: "Những thứ này ngươi [đem] để làm gì?" Xíp-ba nói: "Lừa [là] để cho gia đình vua cưỡi, bánh và trái cây mùa hạ để cho các thanh niên ăn, còn rượu để cho người mệt lả trong hoang mạc uống."
vi.B: Vua hỏi Xíp-ba: "Ngươi đem những thứ này để làm gì?" Xíp-ba thưa: "Lừa để hoàng gia cưỡi, bánh và trái cây mùa hạ để các chiến sĩ ăn, còn rượu cho những ai kiệt sức trong hoang mạc uống."
vi.R: Vua hỏi Xíp-ba: "Những thứ này để làm gì?" Xíp-ba thưa: "Lừa để gia đình đức vua cưỡi. Bánh và trái cây để những người lính trẻ của đức vua ăn. Còn rượu cho những ai bị mệt lả trong sa mạc uống."

ko.L: 왕이 시바에게 말했다. "이것들은 너에게 무엇이냐?" 시바가 말했다. "나귀들은 왕의 집안이 타실 것이고, 빵과 여름 과일은 젊은이들이 먹을 것이고, 포도주는 광야에서 지친 사람이 마실 것입니다."
ko.B: 왕이 시바에게 물었다. "이것들을 왜 가져왔느냐?" 시바가 대답했다. "나귀들은 임금님의 집안이 타시라고 가져왔고, 빵과 여름 과일은 젊은이들이 먹으라고, 포도주는 광야에서 지친 사람이 마시라고 가져왔습니다."
ko.R: 왕이 시바에게 물었다. "이것들은 무엇에 쓰려는 것이냐?" 시바가 대답했다. "나귀는 임금님의 가족이 타실 것입니다. 빵과 과일은 임금님의 젊은 병사들이 먹을 것입니다. 포도주는 광야에서 힘이 빠지고 지친 사람이 마실 것입니다."

decisions.choice: what are these to you: what do you mean by these?
decisions.reason: The question asks what Ziba intends by bringing all this, not what the things are. The king wants to know why Mephibosheth's steward has come out to him, and Ziba answers by naming whom each gift is for.

decisions.choice: and the bread, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a slightly different spelling at this word; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is the ordinary "and the bread". The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: the young men: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: "Young men" is often used of soldiers or the servants who went with a leader (1 Samuel 21:3-6; 25:5). Here they are the men marching with David.

decisions.choice: the faint in the wilderness: those worn out on the march
decisions.reason: David's company is heading into the dry country between Jerusalem and the Jordan (15:23, 28). Ziba's wine is for anyone who becomes exhausted on the way; verse 14 says they all arrived weary.

decisions.choice: your family; your young men
decisions.reason: Ziba speaks of "the king's household" in the polite third person. Readable puts this in the second person, which is how English speakers address someone directly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאַיֵּ֖ה בֶּן־אֲדֹנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִיבָ֜א אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הִנֵּה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר הַיּ֗וֹם יָשִׁ֤יבוּ לִי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וּת אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king, and where [is the] son of your master? And said Ziba to the king, look, he [is] staying in Jerusalem, for he said, today will give back to me [the] house of Israel [the] kingdom of my father.

en.L: And the king said, "And where [is] the son of your master?" And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will give back to me the kingdom of my father.'"
en.B: The king asked, "And where is your master's grandson?" Ziba answered the king, "He is staying in Jerusalem. He has said, 'Today the house of Israel will give me back my grandfather's kingdom.'"
en.R: "Where is Mephibosheth, your master's grandson?" the king asked. Ziba answered, "He has stayed in Jerusalem. He said, 'Now the people of Israel will give me back the kingdom that belonged to my grandfather Saul.'"

es.L: Y el rey dijo: «¿Y dónde [está] el hijo de tu señor?». Y Siba dijo al rey: «He aquí, él se queda en Jerusalén, porque dijo: “Hoy la casa de Israel me devolverá el reino de mi padre”».
es.B: El rey le preguntó: «¿Y dónde está el nieto de tu señor?». Siba le respondió al rey: «Se ha quedado en Jerusalén. Ha dicho: “Hoy la casa de Israel me devolverá el reino de mi abuelo”».
es.R: «¿Dónde está Mefiboset, el nieto de tu señor?», le preguntó el rey. Siba respondió: «Se quedó en Jerusalén. Dijo: “Ahora el pueblo de Israel me devolverá el reino que era de mi abuelo Saúl”».

fr.L: Et le roi dit : « Et où [est] le fils de ton maître ? » Et Tsiba dit au roi : « Voici, il reste à Jérusalem, car il a dit : “Aujourd’hui la maison d’Israël me rendra le royaume de mon père.” »
fr.B: Le roi demanda : « Et où est le petit-fils de ton maître ? » Tsiba répondit au roi : « Il est resté à Jérusalem. Il a dit : “Aujourd’hui, la maison d’Israël va me rendre le royaume de mon grand-père.” »
fr.R: « Où est Mephibosheth, le petit-fils de ton maître ? » a demandé le roi. Tsiba a répondu : « Il est resté à Jérusalem. Il a dit : “Maintenant, le peuple d’Israël va me rendre le royaume qui appartenait à mon grand-père Saül.” »

sw.L: Mfalme akasema, "Na yuko wapi mwana wa bwana wako?" Siba akamwambia mfalme, "Tazama, amebaki Yerusalemu, kwa maana amesema, 'Leo nyumba ya Israeli itanirudishia ufalme wa baba yangu.'"
sw.B: Mfalme akauliza, "Na mjukuu wa bwana wako yuko wapi?" Siba akamjibu mfalme, "Amebaki Yerusalemu. Amesema, 'Leo nyumba ya Israeli itanirudishia ufalme wa babu yangu.'"
sw.R: Mfalme akauliza, "Mefiboshethi, mjukuu wa bwana wako, yuko wapi?" Siba akajibu, "Amebaki Yerusalemu. Amesema, 'Sasa watu wa Israeli watanirudishia ufalme uliokuwa wa babu yangu Sauli.'"

vi.L: Vua nói: "Còn con trai của chủ ngươi đâu?" Xíp-ba nói với vua: "Kìa, cậu ấy ở lại Giê-ru-sa-lem, vì cậu nói: 'Hôm nay nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ trả lại cho ta vương quốc của cha ta.'"
vi.B: Vua hỏi: "Còn cháu của chủ ngươi đâu?" Xíp-ba thưa với vua: "Cậu ấy ở lại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Cậu ấy nói: 'Hôm nay nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ trả lại cho ta vương quốc của ông nội ta.'"
vi.R: Vua hỏi: "Mê-phi-bô-sết, cháu của chủ ngươi, đâu rồi?" Xíp-ba thưa: "Cậu ấy ở lại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Cậu ấy nói: 'Bây giờ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ trả lại cho ta vương quốc của ông nội ta là Sau-lơ.'"

ko.L: 왕이 말했다. "네 주인의 아들은 어디에 있느냐?" 시바가 왕에게 말했다. "보십시오, 그는 예루살렘에 머물러 있습니다. 그가 '오늘 이스라엘 집이 내 아버지의 나라를 나에게 돌려줄 것이다' 하고 말했기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 왕이 물었다. "네 주인의 손자는 어디에 있느냐?" 시바가 왕에게 대답했다. "그는 예루살렘에 남아 있습니다. 그는 '오늘 이스라엘 집안이 내 할아버지의 나라를 나에게 돌려줄 것이다' 하고 말했습니다."
ko.R: 왕이 물었다. "네 주인의 손자 므비보셋은 어디에 있느냐?" 시바가 대답했다. "그는 예루살렘에 남아 있습니다. 그는 '이제 이스라엘 백성이 내 할아버지 사울의 나라를 나에게 돌려줄 것이다' 하고 말했습니다."

decisions.choice: the son of your master; my father: Saul's grandson; Saul
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses "son" and "father" for descendants and ancestors. Ziba's master was Saul, so "the son of your master" is Saul's grandson Mephibosheth, and "my father" in his reported words is Saul, as in 9:7-10.

decisions.choice: Ziba's report: an accusation the reader cannot yet test
decisions.reason: Ziba claims that Mephibosheth stayed behind hoping to win back Saul's throne. When Mephibosheth meets David later, he says Ziba deceived him and left him behind because he was lame (19:25-28). The story gives Ziba's words here without comment.

decisions.choice: the house of Israel; the kingdom: the tribes, and royal rule over them
decisions.reason: "The house of Israel" is the people of the tribes as a whole. With Israel divided between David and Absalom, Ziba makes Mephibosheth hope that the kingdom will return to Saul's line.

decisions.choice: grandson; grandfather
decisions.reason: As in 9:9-10, Balanced and Readable say "grandson" and "grandfather" so the reader does not think of Ziba's own son or Mephibosheth's father Jonathan. Readable also names Mephibosheth and Saul.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְצִבָ֔א הִנֵּ֣ה לְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִמְפִי־בֹ֑שֶׁת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ הִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֔יתִי אֶמְצָא־חֵ֥ן בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Ziba, look, to you [is] all that [belonged] to Mephibosheth. And said Ziba, I bow down; may I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.

en.L: And the king said to Ziba, "Look, all that belonged to Mephibosheth [is] yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down. May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."
en.B: Then the king said to Ziba, "Everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." Ziba said, "I bow before you. May I find favor with you, my lord the king."
en.R: The king told Ziba, "Then everything Mephibosheth owned now belongs to you." Ziba said, "I bow down to you, my lord the king. I hope you will be pleased with me."

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Siba: «He aquí, tuyo [es] todo lo que [era] de Mefiboset». Y Siba dijo: «Me postro. Halle yo gracia ante tus ojos, mi señor el rey».
es.B: Entonces el rey le dijo a Siba: «Todo lo que era de Mefiboset ahora es tuyo». Siba dijo: «Me inclino ante ti. Que yo halle gracia ante ti, mi señor el rey».
es.R: El rey le dijo a Siba: «Entonces todo lo que tenía Mefiboset ahora es tuyo». Siba dijo: «Me inclino ante ti, mi señor el rey. Espero que estés contento conmigo».

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Tsiba : « Voici, tout ce qui [était] à Mephibosheth [est] à toi. » Et Tsiba dit : « Je me prosterne ! Que je trouve grâce à tes yeux, mon seigneur le roi ! »
fr.B: Alors le roi dit à Tsiba : « Tout ce qui appartenait à Mephibosheth est désormais à toi. » Tsiba dit : « Je me prosterne devant toi. Que je trouve grâce à tes yeux, mon seigneur le roi ! »
fr.R: Le roi a dit à Tsiba : « Alors tout ce qui appartenait à Mephibosheth est maintenant à toi. » Tsiba a dit : « Je m’incline devant toi, mon seigneur le roi. J’espère que tu seras toujours content de moi. »

sw.L: Mfalme akamwambia Siba, "Tazama, vyote vilivyokuwa vya Mefiboshethi [ni] vyako." Siba akasema, "Ninasujudu. Nipate kibali machoni pako, bwana wangu mfalme."
sw.B: Ndipo mfalme akamwambia Siba, "Kila kitu kilichokuwa cha Mefiboshethi sasa ni chako." Siba akasema, "Ninasujudu mbele yako. Nipate kibali kwako, bwana wangu mfalme."
sw.R: Mfalme akamwambia Siba, "Basi kila kitu alichokuwa nacho Mefiboshethi sasa ni chako." Siba akasema, "Ninakusujudia, bwana wangu mfalme. Natumaini utaendelea kupendezwa nami."

vi.L: Vua nói với Xíp-ba: "Kìa, mọi thứ thuộc về Mê-phi-bô-sết [là] của ngươi." Xíp-ba nói: "Tôi xin cúi lạy; nguyện tôi được ơn trước mắt vua, thưa chúa tôi là vua."
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua bảo Xíp-ba: "Từ nay mọi thứ của Mê-phi-bô-sết đều thuộc về ngươi." Xíp-ba thưa: "Tôi xin cúi lạy bệ hạ. Nguyện tôi luôn được bệ hạ đoái thương."
vi.R: Vua bảo Xíp-ba: "Vậy thì mọi thứ của Mê-phi-bô-sết từ nay thuộc về ngươi." Xíp-ba thưa: "Thưa đức vua, tôi xin cúi lạy đức vua. Mong đức vua luôn hài lòng về tôi."

ko.L: 왕이 시바에게 말했다. "보아라, 므비보셋에게 속한 것이 모두 네 것이다." 시바가 말했다. "제가 엎드려 절합니다. 내 주 임금님, 제가 임금님의 눈에 은혜를 입기를 바랍니다."
ko.B: 그러자 왕이 시바에게 말했다. "므비보셋의 것은 이제 모두 네 것이다." 시바가 말했다. "임금님께 엎드려 절합니다. 내 주 임금님, 늘 저를 좋게 보아 주십시오."
ko.R: 왕이 시바에게 말했다. "그렇다면 므비보셋이 가진 것은 이제 모두 네 것이다." 시바가 말했다. "내 주 임금님, 엎드려 절합니다. 임금님께서 저를 좋게 여겨 주시기를 바랍니다."

decisions.choice: the king gives Mephibosheth's estate to Ziba
decisions.reason: David acts at once on Ziba's word, with no chance for Mephibosheth to answer. He later divides the land between them, unsure whom to believe (19:30).

decisions.choice: I bow down: said as he does it
decisions.reason: The verb form says the act is done in the speaking: Ziba bows as he says it, a sign of thanks and submission.

decisions.choice: find favor in your eyes: keep your goodwill
decisions.reason: To "find favor in someone's eyes" is to be looked on kindly by them (Genesis 6:8; 1 Samuel 20:3). Ziba hopes to keep the king's goodwill.

decisions.choice: I hope you will be pleased with me
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom "find favor in your eyes" (m3) in plain words.

source.text: וּבָ֛א הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַד־בַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשָּׁם֩ אִ֨ישׁ יוֹצֵ֜א מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת בֵּית־שָׁא֗וּל וּשְׁמוֹ֙ שִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־גֵּרָ֔א יֹצֵ֥א יָצ֖וֹא וּמְקַלֵּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And came King David to Bahurim, and look, from there a man coming out from [the] clan of [the] house of Saul, and his name [was] Shimei son of Gera, coming out, coming out and cursing.

en.L: And King David came to Bahurim, and look, from there a man was coming out, from the clan of the house of Saul, and his name [was] Shimei son of Gera. He came out, coming out and cursing.
en.B: As King David reached Bahurim, a man from the clan of Saul's family came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he came out he kept cursing.
en.R: When King David came to the town of Bahurim, a man came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he was from Saul's clan. As he came, he kept shouting curses at David.

es.L: Y el rey David llegó hasta Bahurim, y he aquí, salía de allí un hombre del clan de la casa de Saúl, y su nombre [era] Simei hijo de Gera. Salía, salía y maldecía.
es.B: Cuando el rey David llegó a Bahurim, salió de allí un hombre del clan de la familia de Saúl. Se llamaba Simei hijo de Gera, y mientras salía no paraba de maldecir.
es.R: Cuando el rey David llegó al pueblo de Bahurim, salió de allí un hombre. Se llamaba Simei hijo de Gera, y era del clan de Saúl. Mientras se acercaba, no paraba de gritarle maldiciones a David.

fr.L: Et le roi David arriva jusqu’à Bahourim, et voici, de là sortit un homme du clan de la maison de Saül, et son nom [était] Shiméï, fils de Guéra ; il sortait, sortait en maudissant.
fr.B: Comme le roi David arrivait à Bahourim, un homme du clan de la famille de Saül en sortit. Il s’appelait Shiméï, fils de Guéra, et tout en sortant il ne cessait de maudire.
fr.R: Quand le roi David est arrivé près de la ville de Bahourim, un homme est sorti de là. Il s’appelait Shiméï, fils de Guéra, et il était du clan de Saül. En s’approchant, il criait sans arrêt des malédictions contre David.

sw.L: Mfalme Daudi akafika Bahurimu, na tazama, kutoka huko mtu mmoja alikuwa akitoka, wa ukoo wa nyumba ya Sauli, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Shimei mwana wa Gera. Akatoka, akitoka na kulaani.
sw.B: Mfalme Daudi alipofika Bahurimu, mtu mmoja wa ukoo wa jamaa ya Sauli akatoka huko. Jina lake lilikuwa Shimei mwana wa Gera, na alipokuwa akitoka aliendelea kulaani.
sw.R: Mfalme Daudi alipofika katika mji wa Bahurimu, mtu mmoja akatoka huko. Jina lake lilikuwa Shimei mwana wa Gera, naye alikuwa wa ukoo wa Sauli. Alipokuwa akija, aliendelea kumtupia Daudi laana kwa sauti.

vi.L: Vua Đa-vít đến Ba-hu-rim, thì kìa, từ đó có một người thuộc dòng họ nhà Sau-lơ đi ra, tên [là] Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra. Ông vừa đi ra vừa nguyền rủa.
vi.B: Khi vua Đa-vít đến Ba-hu-rim, có một người thuộc dòng họ nhà Sau-lơ từ đó đi ra. Người ấy tên là Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra, vừa đi ra vừa nguyền rủa không ngớt.
vi.R: Khi vua Đa-vít đến làng Ba-hu-rim, có một người từ đó đi ra. Người ấy tên là Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra, thuộc dòng họ Sau-lơ. Vừa đi, ông ta vừa la lối nguyền rủa Đa-vít.

ko.L: 다윗 왕이 바후림에 이르렀을 때, 보라, 거기에서 사울 집안의 친족인 한 사람이 나왔는데, 그의 이름은 게라의 아들 시므이였다. 그는 나오면서 계속 저주했다.
ko.B: 다윗 왕이 바후림에 이르렀을 때, 사울 집안의 친족 한 사람이 거기에서 나왔다. 그의 이름은 게라의 아들 시므이였는데, 그는 나오면서 줄곧 저주를 퍼부었다.
ko.R: 다윗 왕이 바후림 마을에 이르렀을 때 한 사람이 그곳에서 나왔다. 그의 이름은 게라의 아들 시므이였는데, 사울 집안 사람이었다. 시므이는 다가오면서 다윗에게 계속 저주를 퍼부었다.

decisions.choice: Bahurim: a village of Benjamin east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Bahurim lay on the road from Jerusalem down to the Jordan, in the land of Benjamin, Saul's tribe (3:16; 17:18; 19:17). Shimei's home was there (1 Kings 2:8).

decisions.choice: coming out, coming out and cursing: he kept on cursing as he came
decisions.reason: The verb "come out" is doubled and joined to "cursing". The form shows action going on: Shimei did not curse once but kept it up as he came out and followed along (verse 13).

decisions.choice: cursing: calling down harm on David and treating him with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to make light of someone and to wish ruin on them. To curse the ruler of God's people was forbidden (Exodus 22:27), so Shimei's words were a serious crime, as Abishai says in verse 9.

decisions.choice: the town of Bahurim; at David
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bahurim was a town and that David was the one being cursed, as verses 6-7 make plain.

decisions.choice: Bahourim, Shiméï fils de Guéra
decisions.reason: Shiméï as the Samuel terms note; Bahourim and Guéra follow the French spelling of the Hebrew sounds ("ou", "gu"); kept for both books.

decisions.choice: Bahurim; Simei hijo de Gera
decisions.reason: Simei as the terms note; Bahurim and Gera keep their usual Spanish spelling.

decisions.choice: "Ba-hu-rim"; "Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra"
decisions.reason: Names as the Samuel terms note gives them, with the usual Vietnamese forms of Bahurim and Gera.

source.text: וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔ד וְאֶת־כָּל־עַבְדֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וְכָל־הָעָם֙ וְכָל־הַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he stoned with stones David and all [the] servants of the king David, and all the people and all the mighty men [were] on his right and on his left.

en.L: And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David, and all the people and all the mighty men [were] on his right and on his left.
en.B: He threw stones at David and at all King David's officials, even though all the people and all the warriors were on David's right and on his left.
en.R: He threw stones at David and at all the king's officials. He did this even though David was surrounded on both sides by his people and his best soldiers.

es.L: Y arrojaba piedras contra David y contra todos los siervos del rey David, y todo el pueblo y todos los valientes [estaban] a su derecha y a su izquierda.
es.B: Le arrojaba piedras a David y a todos los oficiales del rey David, aunque todo el pueblo y todos los guerreros estaban a la derecha y a la izquierda de David.
es.R: Le tiraba piedras a David y a todos los oficiales del rey. Lo hacía aunque David estaba rodeado por todos lados de su gente y de sus mejores soldados.

fr.L: Et il lança des pierres contre David et contre tous les serviteurs du roi David, et tout le peuple et tous les vaillants hommes [étaient] à sa droite et à sa gauche.
fr.B: Il lançait des pierres contre David et contre tous les officiers du roi David, alors que tout le peuple et tous les guerriers d’élite entouraient David à droite et à gauche.
fr.R: Il a lancé des pierres contre David et contre tous les officiers du roi. Il faisait cela alors que David était entouré, des deux côtés, par son peuple et ses meilleurs soldats.

sw.L: Akawatupia mawe Daudi na watumishi wote wa Mfalme Daudi, na watu wote na mashujaa wote [walikuwa] upande wake wa kulia na upande wake wa kushoto.
sw.B: Akawatupia mawe Daudi na maafisa wote wa Mfalme Daudi, ingawa watu wote na mashujaa wote walikuwa upande wa kulia wa Daudi na upande wake wa kushoto.
sw.R: Akamtupia Daudi mawe pamoja na maafisa wote wa mfalme. Alifanya hivyo ingawa Daudi alikuwa amezungukwa pande zote mbili na watu wake na askari wake hodari kuliko wote.

vi.L: Ông ném đá vào Đa-vít và vào tất cả các đầy tớ của vua Đa-vít, dù toàn dân và tất cả các dũng sĩ [đều ở] bên phải và bên trái vua.
vi.B: Ông ta ném đá vào Đa-vít và tất cả quần thần của vua Đa-vít, dù toàn dân và tất cả các dũng sĩ đều ở bên phải và bên trái Đa-vít.
vi.R: Ông ta ném đá vào Đa-vít và tất cả quần thần của vua. Ông ta làm thế dù hai bên Đa-vít có dân chúng và những chiến binh giỏi nhất của vua.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 다윗과 다윗 왕의 모든 신하에게 돌을 던졌다. 온 백성과 모든 용사가 그의 오른쪽과 왼쪽에 있었다.
ko.B: 그는 다윗과 다윗 왕의 모든 신하에게 돌을 던졌다. 온 백성과 모든 용사가 다윗의 오른쪽과 왼쪽에 있었는데도 그렇게 했다.
ko.R: 시므이는 다윗과 왕의 모든 신하에게 돌을 던졌다. 다윗의 양쪽에 백성과 가장 뛰어난 군인들이 둘러서 있었는데도 그렇게 했다.

decisions.choice: and all the people ... on his right and on his left: although David was well guarded
decisions.reason: The last clause describes the scene: David walked with his people and his warriors close around him. Shimei threw stones all the same, from across the slope (verse 13). The clause shows how bold and how hostile he was.

decisions.choice: the mighty men: David's elite warriors
decisions.reason: The word names proven fighters. David had a well-known band of them (10:7; 23:8-39), and they now guarded the king as he fled.

decisions.choice: the people: everyone who left Jerusalem with David
decisions.reason: Here "the people" is not only soldiers: David's household and many others had gone out with him (15:16-17, 23, 30).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As set for these books, "the king's servants" in the sense of his court is "officials" at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: David's right; on both sides
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David, so "his" is not taken as Shimei; Readable says "both sides" for "right and left".

source.text: וְכֹֽה־אָמַ֥ר שִׁמְעִ֖י בְּקַֽלְל֑וֹ צֵ֥א צֵ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הַדָּמִ֖ים וְאִ֥ישׁ הַבְּלִיָּֽעַל׃

records.literal_gloss: And thus said Shimei in his cursing, get out, get out, man of the bloods and man of the worthlessness.

en.L: And thus Shimei said as he cursed, "Get out, get out, man of blood and man of worthlessness!
en.B: As he cursed, Shimei said, "Get out! Get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!
en.R: This is what Shimei shouted as he cursed: "Get out of here! Get out, you murderer! You wicked man!

es.L: Y así decía Simei mientras maldecía: «¡Fuera, fuera, hombre de sangre y hombre perverso!
es.B: Mientras maldecía, Simei decía: «¡Fuera! ¡Fuera, hombre sanguinario, hombre perverso!
es.R: Esto es lo que gritaba Simei mientras lo maldecía: «¡Vete de aquí! ¡Fuera, asesino! ¡Malvado!

fr.L: Et ainsi parlait Shiméï en maudissant : « Va-t’en, va-t’en, homme de sang et homme de rien !
fr.B: Tout en maudissant, Shiméï disait : « Va-t’en ! Va-t’en, homme sanguinaire, vaurien !
fr.R: Voici ce que Shiméï criait en le maudissant : « Va-t’en d’ici ! Va-t’en, assassin ! Homme mauvais !

sw.L: Shimei akasema hivi alipokuwa akilaani, "Toka, toka, wewe mtu wa damu na mtu wa ubaradhuli!
sw.B: Shimei alipokuwa akilaani, alisema, "Toka! Toka, wewe mtu wa damu, wewe mtu usiyefaa kitu!
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo Shimei alivyopiga kelele alipokuwa akilaani: "Toka hapa! Toka, wewe muuaji! Wewe mtu mwovu!

vi.L: Si-mê-i nguyền rủa như vầy: "Cút đi, cút đi, đồ người máu và người vô lại!
vi.B: Si-mê-i vừa nguyền rủa vừa nói: "Cút đi! Cút đi, đồ khát máu, đồ vô lại!
vi.R: Si-mê-i vừa nguyền rủa vừa la lên: "Cút khỏi đây! Cút đi, đồ sát nhân! Đồ gian ác!

ko.L: 시므이가 저주하며 이렇게 말했다. "꺼져라, 꺼져라, 피의 사람아, 쓸모없는 자야!
ko.B: 시므이는 저주하며 말했다. "꺼져라! 꺼져라, 이 피비린내 나는 자야, 이 불량배야!
ko.R: 시므이는 저주를 퍼부으며 이렇게 소리쳤다. "여기서 꺼져라! 꺼져라, 이 살인자야! 이 악한 놈아!

decisions.choice: man of blood: a man guilty of shedding blood
decisions.reason: The plural of "blood" is used for blood that has been shed and the guilt it brings (Exodus 22:1; Psalm 5:7). Shimei calls David a murderer, and in verse 8 he says whose blood he means.

decisions.choice: man of worthlessness: a worthless, wicked man
decisions.reason: As in Judges 19:22 and 1 Samuel 25:17, the noun (beliyya'al) means worthlessness or ruin, and the phrase names a man who is good for nothing and does harm. It is one of the strongest insults in Hebrew.

decisions.choice: get out, get out: go away for good
decisions.reason: The doubled command is urgent and scornful. Shimei is glad to see David driven from his city and his throne, and tells him to keep going.

decisions.choice: worthless man (B); wicked man (R)
decisions.reason: As in Judges 19:22: Balanced says "worthless man" and Readable "wicked man"; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: murderer
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "man of blood" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: hombre perverso (L, B); malvado (R)
decisions.reason: The 'man of worthlessness' is the word behind 'hombres perversos' in the terms note ('sons of Belial'); Literal and Balanced keep 'perverso', Readable says 'malvado', as the English 'wicked man'.

decisions.choice: mtu wa ubaradhuli (L); mtu usiyefaa kitu (B); mtu mwovu (R)
decisions.reason: "Man of worthlessness" uses the Hebrew word behind "sons of Belial"; the Samuel terms note has "watu wasiofaa kitu" for that phrase, which Balanced follows. Literal keeps a noun, "ubaradhuli" (worthlessness, wickedness); Readable says "wicked" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "đồ ..." for Shimei's insults, and "ngươi" for David in his mouth
decisions.reason: The scornful "đồ" carries his contempt; he refuses the king any title. "kẻ vô lại" is the Samuel terms note's word for *beliyyaʿal*.

decisions.choice: Shimei shouts at the king in the plain style (해라체), with "꺼져라" and "-야"
decisions.reason: Cursing the king, Shimei drops every courtesy a subject owes him; the plain style and the insulting vocative "-야" carry his contempt.

decisions.choice: "불량배" for "man of worthlessness"
decisions.reason: The terms of this translation use "불량배" for the "sons of Belial" phrase in 1 and 2 Samuel; Literal keeps the plainer "쓸모없는 자" and Readable "악한 놈", as the English levels differ.

source.text: הֵשִׁיב֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ יְהוָ֜ה כֹּ֣ל׀דְּמֵ֣י בֵית־שָׁא֗וּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַ֨כְתָּ֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בְּנֶ֑ךָ וְהִנְּךָ֙ בְּרָ֣עָתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ דָּמִ֖ים אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has brought back on you Yahweh all [the] bloods of [the] house of Saul, in whose place you reigned, and has given Yahweh the kingdom into [the] hand of Absalom your son, and look, you [are] in your calamity, for a man of bloods you [are].

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And look, you [are] in your calamity, for you [are] a man of blood!"
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has paid you back for all the blood of Saul's family, whose throne you took. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has handed the kingdom over to your son Absalom. And see, disaster has caught you, because you are a man of blood!"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is punishing you for all the people in Saul's family you killed. You took Saul's place as king, and now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given the kingdom to your son Absalom. Look at the trouble you are in! It has happened because you are a murderer!"

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hecho volver sobre ti toda la sangre de la casa de Saúl, en cuyo lugar has reinado, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado el reino en mano de Absalón tu hijo. Y he aquí, [estás] en tu desgracia, porque [eres] un hombre de sangre».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha hecho pagar toda la sangre de la familia de Saúl, cuyo trono tomaste. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado el reino a tu hijo Absalón. ¡Mira, la desgracia te ha alcanzado, porque eres un hombre sanguinario!».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te está castigando por toda la gente de la familia de Saúl que mataste. Tú le quitaste el lugar a Saúl como rey, y ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha dado el reino a tu hijo Absalón. ¡Mira en qué problema estás metido! ¡Te ha pasado porque eres un asesino!».

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait retomber sur toi tout le sang de la maison de Saül, à la place duquel tu as régné, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a livré le royaume entre les mains d’Absalom ton fils. Et te voici dans ton malheur, car tu [es] un homme de sang ! »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te fait payer tout le sang de la famille de Saül, dont tu as pris le trône. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a remis le royaume à ton fils Absalom. Te voilà pris dans le malheur, car tu es un homme sanguinaire ! »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te punit pour tous les membres de la famille de Saül que tu as tués. Tu as pris la place de Saül comme roi, et maintenant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné le royaume à ton fils Absalom. Regarde dans quel malheur tu es ! Cela t’arrive parce que tu es un assassin ! »

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekurudishia damu yote ya nyumba ya Sauli, ambaye ulitawala mahali pake, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameutia ufalme mkononi mwa Absalomu mwanao. Na tazama, wewe [u] katika msiba wako, kwa maana wewe [ni] mtu wa damu!"
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekulipiza damu yote ya jamaa ya Sauli, ambaye ulimnyang'anya kiti chake cha enzi. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameutia ufalme mikononi mwa mwanao Absalomu. Na tazama, maafa yamekupata, kwa sababu wewe ni mtu wa damu!"
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakuadhibu kwa ajili ya watu wote wa jamaa ya Sauli uliowaua. Ulichukua nafasi ya Sauli kama mfalme, na sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempa mwanao Absalomu ufalme. Tazama taabu uliyomo! Imekupata kwa sababu wewe ni muuaji!"

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đổ lại trên ngươi tất cả máu của nhà Sau-lơ, là người mà ngươi đã cướp ngôi; và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trao vương quốc vào tay Áp-sa-lôm con trai ngươi. Kìa, ngươi [đang] gặp tai họa, vì ngươi [là] người máu!"
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo trả ngươi về tất cả máu của nhà Sau-lơ, người mà ngươi đã cướp ngôi. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trao vương quốc vào tay Áp-sa-lôm con trai ngươi. Kìa, tai họa đã đến với ngươi, vì ngươi là kẻ khát máu!"
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang phạt ngươi vì tất cả những người trong nhà Sau-lơ mà ngươi đã giết. Ngươi đã chiếm ngôi vua của Sau-lơ, và bây giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trao vương quốc cho Áp-sa-lôm con trai ngươi. Hãy xem ngươi đang gặp nạn kìa! Đó là vì ngươi là kẻ sát nhân!"

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 네가 그 대신 왕이 된 사울 집안의 모든 피를 너에게 갚으셨다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 나라를 네 아들 압살롬의 손에 넘기셨다. 보아라, 너는 재앙을 만났다. 너는 피의 사람이기 때문이다!"
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사울 집안의 피를 모두 너에게 되갚으셨다. 너는 사울의 왕위를 빼앗았지만, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 나라를 네 아들 압살롬에게 넘겨주셨다. 보아라, 네가 재앙을 만났다. 너는 피비린내 나는 자이기 때문이다!"
ko.R: 네가 사울 집안 사람들을 죽였으니, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 벌을 내리신다. 너는 사울의 자리를 빼앗아 왕이 되었지만, 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 나라를 네 아들 압살롬에게 주셨다. 네가 어떤 재앙을 만났는지 보아라! 네가 살인자이기 때문에 이렇게 된 것이다!"

decisions.choice: all the blood of the house of Saul: deaths Shimei blames on David
decisions.reason: Shimei may have in mind Abner and Ish-bosheth, who were killed while David was making his claim to the throne (3:27; 4:5-8). The story has shown that David had no part in those deaths and mourned them (3:28-39; 4:9-12). Shimei, of Saul's clan, sees David's fall as payment for them; the reader knows the charge is false, though David has blood on his hands in another matter (11:14-17; 12:9-10).

decisions.choice: brought back on you: repaid you for
decisions.reason: To bring someone's blood "back on" him is to make the guilt of a killing fall on the one who did it (1 Kings 2:32-33). Shimei claims the LORD is punishing David.

decisions.choice: your calamity: the disaster that has come on you
decisions.reason: The noun means harm or disaster, and can also mean evil done. Shimei uses it of David's ruin, which he says David brought on himself.

decisions.choice: for all the people in Saul's family you killed
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what Shimei's charge "the blood of the house of Saul" means. It reports his accusation; it is not the narrator's verdict (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־צְרוּיָה֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֣מָּה יְקַלֵּ֞ל הַכֶּ֤לֶב הַמֵּת֙ הַזֶּ֔ה אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֶעְבְּרָה־נָּ֖א וְאָסִ֥ירָה אֶת־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Abishai son of Zeruiah to the king, why will curse this dead dog my lord the king? Let me go over, please, and let me take off his head.

en.L: And Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over, please, and take off his head."
en.B: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why let this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me cross over and cut off his head."
en.R: Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "My lord the king, why should this dead dog be allowed to curse you? Let me go over there and cut off his head!"

es.L: Y Abisai hijo de Sarvia dijo al rey: «¿Por qué ha de maldecir este perro muerto a mi señor el rey? Te ruego que me dejes pasar y quitarle la cabeza».
es.B: Entonces Abisai hijo de Sarvia le dijo al rey: «¿Por qué dejar que este perro muerto maldiga a mi señor el rey? Déjame cruzar, te lo ruego, y cortarle la cabeza».
es.R: Abisai hijo de Sarvia le dijo al rey: «Mi señor el rey, ¿por qué dejar que este perro muerto te maldiga? ¡Déjame ir allá y cortarle la cabeza!».

fr.L: Et Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, dit au roi : « Pourquoi ce chien mort maudirait-il mon seigneur le roi ? Laisse-moi passer, je te prie, et lui enlever la tête. »
fr.B: Alors Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, dit au roi : « Pourquoi laisser ce chien mort maudire mon seigneur le roi ? Permets-moi de traverser et de lui couper la tête. »
fr.R: Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, a dit au roi : « Mon seigneur le roi, pourquoi laisser ce chien mort te maudire ? Laisse-moi aller là-bas lui couper la tête ! »

sw.L: Abishai mwana wa Seruya akamwambia mfalme, "Kwa nini mbwa huyu mfu amlaani bwana wangu mfalme? Tafadhali niache nivuke niondoe kichwa chake."
sw.B: Ndipo Abishai mwana wa Seruya akamwambia mfalme, "Kwa nini umwache mbwa huyu mfu amlaani bwana wangu mfalme? Tafadhali niruhusu nivuke nikakate kichwa chake."
sw.R: Abishai mwana wa Seruya akamwambia mfalme, "Bwana wangu mfalme, kwa nini mbwa huyu mfu aachwe akulaani? Niache niende huko nikakate kichwa chake!"

vi.L: A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia nói với vua: "Sao để con chó chết này nguyền rủa chúa tôi là vua? Xin cho tôi đi qua chặt đầu nó."
vi.B: Bấy giờ A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia tâu với vua: "Sao lại để con chó chết này nguyền rủa bệ hạ? Xin cho tôi qua đó chặt đầu nó."
vi.R: A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia thưa với vua: "Thưa đức vua, sao lại để con chó chết này nguyền rủa đức vua? Xin cho tôi qua đó chặt đầu nó!"

ko.L: 스루야의 아들 아비새가 왕에게 말했다. "어찌하여 이 죽은 개가 내 주 임금님을 저주하게 [두십니까]? 부디 제가 건너가서 그의 머리를 베게 해 주십시오."
ko.B: 그러자 스루야의 아들 아비새가 왕에게 말했다. "이 죽은 개가 내 주 임금님을 저주하게 내버려 두실 겁니까? 제가 건너가서 저놈의 목을 베게 해 주십시오."
ko.R: 스루야의 아들 아비새가 왕에게 말했다. "내 주 임금님, 왜 이 죽은 개 같은 놈이 임금님을 저주하게 내버려 두십니까? 제가 건너가서 저놈의 목을 베어 버리겠습니다!"

decisions.choice: dead dog: a man of no worth at all
decisions.reason: To call someone a dead dog is to say he is worth nothing. David used it of himself before Saul (1 Samuel 24:15) and Mephibosheth of himself before David (9:8); Abishai uses it as an insult.

decisions.choice: cursing the king: a crime that deserved death
decisions.reason: The law forbade cursing a ruler of the people (Exodus 22:27; compare 1 Kings 21:10). Abishai thinks Shimei has earned death, and David later says the same before his death (1 Kings 2:8-9).

decisions.choice: Abishai son of Zeruiah: David's nephew, Joab's brother
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel were among David's leading men (2:18). Abishai had once offered to kill Saul in the same spirit (1 Samuel 26:8).

decisions.choice: go over: cross to where Shimei is
decisions.reason: Shimei was walking along the hillside across from David (verse 13). Abishai asks to cross over to him.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה־לִּ֥י וְלָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י צְרֻיָ֑ה כֹּ֣ה יְקַלֵּ֗ל כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ אָ֤מַר לוֹ֙ קַלֵּ֣ל אֶת־דָּוִ֔ד וּמִ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ עָשִׂ֥יתָה כֵּֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said the king, what [is] to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? Thus he curses, for Yahweh said to him, curse David; and who will say, why have you done so?

en.L: But the king said, "What [is there] to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? So let him curse, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said to him, 'Curse David.' And who shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"
en.B: But the king said, "What does this have to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse like this, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told him, 'Curse David.' Who then can ask, 'Why have you done this?'"
en.R: But the king answered, "Sons of Zeruiah, keep out of this. Let him go on cursing. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has told him to curse David. So who can ask him, 'Why are you doing this?'"

es.L: Pero el rey dijo: «¿Qué [hay] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y yo, hijos de Sarvia? Que maldiga así, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha dicho: “Maldice a David”. ¿Y quién dirá: “¿Por qué has hecho así?”».
es.B: Pero el rey dijo: «¿Qué tiene esto que ver con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hijos de Sarvia? Que maldiga así, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha dicho: “Maldice a David”. ¿Quién puede entonces preguntarle: “¿Por qué has hecho esto?”».
es.R: Pero el rey respondió: «Hijos de Sarvia, no se {{plural_you:metan|metáis}} en esto. {{plural_you:Déjenlo|Dejadlo}} que siga maldiciendo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha dicho que maldiga a David. Entonces, ¿quién puede preguntarle: “¿Por qué haces esto?”».

fr.L: Mais le roi dit : « Qu’[y a-t-il] entre moi et vous, fils de Tserouya ? Qu’il maudisse ainsi, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : “Maudis David.” Et qui dira : “Pourquoi as-tu agi ainsi ?” »
fr.B: Mais le roi dit : « En quoi cela vous regarde-t-il, fils de Tserouya ? Qu’il maudisse ainsi, puisque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : “Maudis David.” Qui donc pourrait lui demander : “Pourquoi as-tu fait cela ?” »
fr.R: Mais le roi a répondu : « Fils de Tserouya, ne vous mêlez pas de cela. Laissez-le continuer à maudire. C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui lui a dit de maudire David. Alors, qui peut lui demander : “Pourquoi fais-tu cela ?” »

sw.L: Lakini mfalme akasema, "Kuna [nini] kati yangu na ninyi, wana wa Seruya? Basi na alaani, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia, 'Mlaani Daudi.' Na ni nani atakayesema, 'Kwa nini umefanya hivyo?'"
sw.B: Lakini mfalme akasema, "Jambo hili linawahusu nini ninyi, wana wa Seruya? Mwacheni alaani hivyo, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia, 'Mlaani Daudi.' Basi ni nani awezaye kuuliza, 'Kwa nini umefanya hivi?'"
sw.R: Lakini mfalme akajibu, "Wana wa Seruya, msiingilie jambo hili. Mwacheni aendelee kulaani. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia amlaani Daudi. Basi ni nani awezaye kumwuliza, 'Kwa nini unafanya hivi?'"

vi.L: Nhưng vua nói: "Ta với các ngươi có [liên quan] gì, hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia? Cứ để nó nguyền rủa, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với nó: 'Hãy nguyền rủa Đa-vít.' Vậy ai dám nói: 'Sao ngươi làm như vậy?'"
vi.B: Nhưng vua nói: "Hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia, việc này có liên quan gì đến các ngươi? Cứ để nó nguyền rủa như thế, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo nó: 'Hãy nguyền rủa Đa-vít.' Vậy ai dám hỏi: 'Sao ngươi làm như vậy?'"
vi.R: Nhưng vua đáp: "Hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia, đừng can thiệp vào việc này. Cứ để nó nguyền rủa. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo nó nguyền rủa Đa-vít. Vậy ai dám hỏi nó: 'Sao ngươi làm như vậy?'"

ko.L: 그러나 왕이 말했다. "스루야의 아들들아, 나와 너희에게 무슨 [상관이] 있느냐? 그가 저주하게 두어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 '다윗을 저주하여라' 하고 말씀하셨으니, 누가 '어찌하여 네가 이렇게 하느냐?' 하고 말할 수 있겠느냐?"
ko.B: 그러나 왕이 말했다. "스루야의 아들들아, 이것이 너희와 무슨 상관이냐? 그가 저렇게 저주하는 것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 '다윗을 저주하여라' 하고 말씀하셨기 때문이다. 그러니 누가 '왜 이렇게 하느냐?' 하고 물을 수 있겠느냐?"
ko.R: 그러나 왕이 대답했다. "스루야의 아들들아, 너희는 이 일에 끼어들지 마라. 그가 계속 저주하게 두어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 다윗을 저주하라고 말씀하셨다. 그러니 누가 그에게 '왜 이렇게 하느냐?' 하고 물을 수 있겠느냐?"

decisions.choice: what is there to me and to you: this is not your affair
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the speaker apart from the one he speaks to: we do not share this concern, leave it to me (19:23; Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). David refuses Abishai's offer.

decisions.choice: sons of Zeruiah: Abishai and Joab together
decisions.reason: The plural takes in Joab as well as Abishai. David sees both brothers as too quick to kill (3:39; 19:23).

decisions.choice: so let him curse, for the LORD has told him, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: if he curses, and if the LORD has told him
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) has "thus he curses, for the LORD has said". The written consonants (ketiv) read "for he curses, and for the LORD has said", which can be taken as "if he curses, and if the LORD has told him ... who can say ...?" On either reading David leaves Shimei alone and allows that the LORD may be behind the cursing; the written text says it more tentatively.

decisions.choice: the LORD has told him to curse David: David accepts the cursing as coming from God's hand
decisions.reason: David does not say that Shimei is right or that God approves of his hatred. He sees the LORD's hand even in a hostile act, as the trouble Nathan announced for his sin (12:10-11), and he will not strike back at what may be God's discipline. The Bible speaks this way elsewhere of God working through people who act from their own motives (24:1; 1 Kings 22:20-23). David is not certain: in verse 12 he hopes the LORD will see his distress.

decisions.choice: What does this have to do with you (B); keep out of this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1) in words a reader will follow; Literal keeps the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} for the sons of Zeruiah
decisions.reason: David answers Abishai but speaks to 'the sons of Zeruiah', Joab and Abishai together, so the plural takes the plural_you setting.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤ד אֶל־אֲבִישַׁי֙ וְאֶל־כָּל־עֲבָדָ֔יו הִנֵּ֥ה בְנִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־יָצָ֥א מִמֵּעַ֖י מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֑י וְאַ֨ף כִּֽי־עַתָּ֜ה בֶּן־הַיְמִינִ֗י הַנִּ֤חוּ לוֹ֙ וִֽיקַלֵּ֔ל כִּ֥י אָֽמַר־ל֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Abishai and to all his servants, look, my son who came out from my inward parts [is] seeking my life; and how much more now the Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for has told him Yahweh.

en.L: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Look, my son, who came out from my body, is seeking my life; and how much more now this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told him [to].
en.B: David said to Abishai and to all his officials, "Look, my own son, who came from my own body, is trying to kill me. How much more, then, this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told him to.
en.R: Then David said to Abishai and all his officials, "My own son is trying to kill me. So of course this man from the tribe of Benjamin wants to see me dead! Leave him alone. Let him curse me, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him to.

es.L: Y David dijo a Abisai y a todos sus siervos: «He aquí, mi hijo, que salió de mis entrañas, busca mi vida; ¡cuánto más ahora este benjamita! {{plural_you:Déjenlo|Dejadlo}} que maldiga, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se [lo] ha dicho.
es.B: David les dijo a Abisai y a todos sus oficiales: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, mi propio hijo, que salió de mis entrañas, quiere matarme. ¡Cuánto más este benjamita! {{plural_you:Déjenlo|Dejadlo}} que maldiga, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se lo ha dicho.
es.R: Entonces David les dijo a Abisai y a todos sus oficiales: «Mi propio hijo quiere matarme. ¡Con mayor razón este hombre de la tribu de Benjamín quiere verme muerto! {{plural_you:Déjenlo|Dejadlo}} en paz. Que me maldiga, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se lo ha dicho.

fr.L: Et David dit à Abishaï et à tous ses serviteurs : « Voici, mon fils, qui est sorti de mes entrailles, cherche ma vie ; à plus forte raison maintenant ce Benjaminite ! Laissez-le, et qu’il maudisse, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui a dit.
fr.B: David dit à Abishaï et à tous ses officiers : « Voyez, mon propre fils, sorti de mes entrailles, cherche à me tuer. À plus forte raison ce Benjaminite ! Laissez-le maudire, puisque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui a dit.
fr.R: Puis David a dit à Abishaï et à tous ses officiers : « Mon propre fils essaie de me tuer. Alors, bien sûr, cet homme de la tribu de Benjamin veut me voir mort ! Laissez-le. Laissez-le me maudire, car c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui le lui a dit.

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Abishai na watumishi wake wote, "Tazama, mwanangu, aliyetoka viunoni mwangu, anautafuta uhai wangu; sembuse sasa Mbenyamini huyu! Mwacheni alaani, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia [afanye hivyo].
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Abishai na maafisa wake wote, "Tazama, mwanangu mwenyewe, aliyetoka katika mwili wangu, anajaribu kuniua. Sembuse sasa Mbenyamini huyu! Mwacheni alaani, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia afanye hivyo.
sw.R: Kisha Daudi akamwambia Abishai na maafisa wake wote, "Mwanangu mwenyewe anajaribu kuniua. Basi si ajabu mtu huyu wa kabila la Benyamini anataka nife! Mwacheni. Na anilaani, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwambia afanye hivyo.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-sai và tất cả các đầy tớ mình: "Kìa, con trai ta, là đứa ra từ lòng ta, còn tìm hại mạng sống ta; huống chi bây giờ người Bên-gia-min này! Hãy để mặc nó nguyền rủa, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo nó [làm thế].
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-sai và tất cả quần thần: "Kìa, chính con ruột ta, do ta sinh ra, còn tìm cách giết ta, huống chi người Bên-gia-min này! Hãy để mặc nó nguyền rủa, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo nó làm thế.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít nói với A-bi-sai và tất cả quần thần: "Chính con ruột ta còn đang tìm cách giết ta. Vậy thì dĩ nhiên người thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min này muốn thấy ta chết! Hãy để mặc nó. Cứ để nó nguyền rủa ta, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo nó làm thế.

ko.L: 다윗이 아비새와 자기의 모든 신하에게 말했다. "보아라, 내 몸에서 나온 내 아들이 내 목숨을 찾고 있는데, 하물며 지금 이 베냐민 사람이야 [더 말할 것이 있겠느냐]! 그를 내버려 두어 저주하게 하여라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 [그렇게] 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다윗이 아비새와 자기의 모든 신하에게 말했다. "보아라, 내 몸에서 나온 내 친아들도 내 목숨을 노리는데, 하물며 이 베냐민 사람이야 오죽하겠느냐! 그를 내버려 두어 저주하게 하여라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 그렇게 하라고 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 다윗이 아비새와 모든 신하에게 말했다. "내 친아들도 나를 죽이려 하고 있다. 그러니 베냐민 지파 사람인 이 사람이 내가 죽기를 바라는 것은 당연하지 않으냐! 그를 내버려 두어라. 나를 저주하게 두어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 그렇게 하라고 말씀하셨다.

decisions.choice: who came out from my inward parts: my own child
decisions.reason: The inward parts are the body as the source of life. A son who comes from a man's body is his own offspring (7:12; Genesis 15:4).

decisions.choice: seeking my life: trying to kill me
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is to try to kill them (1 Samuel 20:1; 22:23). Absalom's revolt is a threat to David's life, as Ahithophel's plan will show (17:1-4).

decisions.choice: how much more now: if the one, then surely the other
decisions.reason: David argues from the greater to the lesser: if his own son wants him dead, it is no surprise that a man of Saul's tribe, with old grievances, curses him.

decisions.choice: the Benjaminite: a man of Saul's tribe
decisions.reason: Saul was from Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:1-2), and many of that tribe resented David for taking the throne from Saul's house (3:19; 20:1).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, David's court servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: So of course this man ... wants to see me dead!
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the comparison (m3) in a full sentence and explains "Benjaminite".

source.text: אוּלַ֛י יִרְאֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּעֵינִ֑י וְהֵשִׁ֨יב יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת קִלְלָת֖וֹ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps will look Yahweh on my eye, and will return Yahweh to me good in place of his cursing this day.

en.L: Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will look on my eye, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will repay me good in place of his cursing this day."
en.B: Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will look on my distress and repay me with good in place of his cursing today."
en.R: Maybe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will see how I am suffering. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may do good things for me in return for the curses this man is shouting at me today."

es.L: Quizá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mire mi aflicción, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me devuelva bien en lugar de su maldición de este día».
es.B: Quizá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mire mi angustia y me pague con bien las maldiciones de hoy».
es.R: Tal vez {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vea cuánto estoy sufriendo. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quizá me haga bien a cambio de las maldiciones que este hombre me grita hoy».

fr.L: Peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} regardera-t-il mon œil, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me rendra-t-il du bien à la place de sa malédiction de ce jour. »
fr.B: Peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} regardera-t-il ma détresse et me rendra-t-il du bien en échange de ses malédictions d’aujourd’hui. »
fr.R: Peut-être que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} verra combien je souffre. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me fera peut-être du bien en échange des malédictions que cet homme me crie aujourd’hui. »

sw.L: Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalitazama jicho langu, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atanilipa mema badala ya kulaani kwake leo."
sw.B: Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataiangalia taabu yangu na kunilipa mema badala ya laana yake leo."
sw.R: Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataona jinsi ninavyoteseka. Kisha anaweza kunitendea mema badala ya laana ambazo mtu huyu ananitupia leo."

vi.L: Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đoái xem con mắt ta, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ trả lại cho ta điều tốt thay cho lời nguyền rủa của nó hôm nay."
vi.B: Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đoái thấy nỗi khổ của ta và ban phước cho ta thay cho lời nguyền rủa của nó hôm nay."
vi.R: Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ thấy ta đang đau khổ thế nào. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể làm điều tốt cho ta, bù lại những lời nguyền rủa mà người này đang la hét vào ta hôm nay."

ko.L: 혹시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 눈을 보시고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 오늘 그가 저주한 것 대신 나에게 선으로 갚아 주실지 모른다."
ko.B: 혹시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 고통을 보시고, 오늘 그가 퍼붓는 저주 대신 나에게 좋은 것으로 갚아 주실지도 모른다."
ko.R: 어쩌면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내가 고통받는 것을 보실 것이다. 그러면 오늘 이 사람이 나에게 퍼붓는 저주 대신에 나에게 좋은 일을 해 주실지도 모른다."

decisions.choice: on my eye, as the scribes' reading has it: on my tears, my distress
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "on my iniquity"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "on my eye". Some ancient translations, the Greek among them, read "on my affliction", a Hebrew word spelled much like both. "My iniquity" would mean that the LORD will see David's guilt, or perhaps the wrong done to him. "My eye" probably means his tears or his plight, which agrees with the ancient translations. The text here follows the scribes' reading.

decisions.choice: look on my eye: see what I am suffering
decisions.reason: For God to "see" a person's trouble is to take note of it and act (Genesis 29:32; 1 Samuel 1:11). David hopes the LORD will see his weeping and humiliation (15:30).

decisions.choice: perhaps the LORD will repay me good: a hope, not a claim
decisions.reason: David does not demand that God bless him. He leaves the matter with God, as one who can turn a curse into a blessing (Deuteronomy 23:6). The word "perhaps" keeps his trust humble.

decisions.choice: my distress (B); how I am suffering (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the probable sense of "my eye" (m1, m2); Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: the curses this man is shouting at me
decisions.reason: Readable names Shimei as "this man", so "his" is not taken to mean the LORD.

decisions.choice: mi aflicción
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is read as 'my eye', standing for what David suffers, as the English Literal keeps; Spanish 'mire mi ojo' would not read as a figure, so Literal says 'mi aflicción', the sense the English Balanced gives.

source.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו בַּדָּ֑רֶךְסוְשִׁמְעִ֡י הֹלֵךְ֩ בְּצֵ֨לַע הָהָ֜ר לְעֻמָּת֗וֹ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיְקַלֵּ֔ל וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ לְעֻמָּת֔וֹ וְעִפַּ֖ר בֶּעָפָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went David and his men on the road, and Shimei [was] going on [the] side of the hill alongside him, going and cursing, and he threw stones alongside him and dusted with dust.

en.L: And David and his men went on the road, and Shimei was going along the side of the hill alongside him, cursing as he went; and he threw stones alongside him and flung dust.
en.B: So David and his men went on along the road, while Shimei kept pace with him on the hillside across from him, cursing as he went, throwing stones toward him and flinging dust.
en.R: So David and his men kept going along the road. Shimei walked along the hillside across from them. As he went, he kept cursing David and throwing stones and dirt at him.

es.L: Y David y sus hombres iban por el camino, y Simei iba por la ladera del monte frente a él, maldiciendo mientras andaba, y arrojaba piedras frente a él y esparcía polvo.
es.B: Así que David y sus hombres siguieron por el camino, mientras Simei iba por la ladera del monte a la par de él, maldiciendo mientras andaba, arrojándole piedras y echándole polvo.
es.R: Así que David y sus hombres siguieron por el camino. Simei iba por la ladera de enfrente. Mientras caminaba, seguía maldiciendo a David y tirándole piedras y tierra.

fr.L: Et David et ses hommes allaient par le chemin, et Shiméï allait sur le flanc de la colline, à côté de lui, maudissant en marchant ; et il lançait des pierres à côté de lui et jetait de la poussière.
fr.B: David et ses hommes poursuivirent leur route, tandis que Shiméï marchait à sa hauteur sur le flanc de la colline, en face de lui, maudissant, lançant des pierres dans sa direction et jetant de la poussière.
fr.R: David et ses hommes ont donc continué leur chemin. Shiméï marchait sur le flanc de la colline, en face d’eux. Tout en marchant, il continuait à maudire David et à lui lancer des pierres et de la poussière.

sw.L: Daudi na watu wake wakaenda njiani, na Shimei alikuwa akienda kando ya kilima sambamba naye, akilaani alipokuwa akienda; akarusha mawe sambamba naye na kutupa mavumbi.
sw.B: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaendelea na njia yao, huku Shimei akienda sambamba naye kwenye mteremko wa kilima upande wa pili, akilaani alipokuwa akienda, akimtupia mawe na kurusha mavumbi.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaendelea kwenda njiani. Shimei akatembea kwenye mteremko wa kilima upande wa pili wao. Alipokuwa akienda, aliendelea kumlaani Daudi na kumtupia mawe na mavumbi.

vi.L: Đa-vít và người của vua đi trên đường, còn Si-mê-i đi dọc theo sườn đồi song song với vua, vừa đi vừa nguyền rủa, ném đá và tung bụi về phía vua.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít và người của vua tiếp tục đi theo đường cái, còn Si-mê-i thì đi trên sườn đồi đối diện, vừa đi vừa nguyền rủa, ném đá về phía vua và tung bụi lên.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và người của vua tiếp tục đi theo con đường. Si-mê-i đi dọc theo sườn đồi phía bên kia. Vừa đi, ông ta vừa nguyền rủa Đa-vít, ném đá và đất cát vào vua.

ko.L: 다윗과 그의 부하들이 길을 가는데, 시므이는 산비탈을 따라 그와 나란히 가면서 저주하고, 그와 나란히 [가면서] 돌을 던지고 흙먼지를 뿌렸다.
ko.B: 다윗과 그의 부하들은 계속 길을 갔다. 시므이는 맞은편 산비탈을 따라 다윗과 나란히 가면서 저주를 퍼붓고, 다윗 쪽으로 돌을 던지고 흙먼지를 뿌렸다.
ko.R: 다윗과 그의 부하들은 계속 길을 갔다. 시므이는 맞은편 산비탈을 따라 걸었다. 그는 가면서 계속 다윗을 저주하고, 다윗에게 돌과 흙을 던졌다.

decisions.choice: the side of the hill: the slope running beside the road
decisions.reason: The word means a side or rib, here the flank of a hill. Shimei walked along the slope above the road, out of easy reach but close enough to be heard.

decisions.choice: alongside him: keeping level with David
decisions.reason: The phrase means "over against" or "corresponding to". Shimei kept pace with David the whole way, so the cursing went on as long as David walked.

decisions.choice: flung dust: a gesture of scorn and rage
decisions.reason: Throwing dust into the air or at someone showed fury and contempt. With the stones, it was meant to shame the king in front of his people.

decisions.choice: throwing stones and dirt at him
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two actions in one plain phrase.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ עֲיֵפִ֑ים וַיִּנָּפֵ֖שׁ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the king and all the people who [were] with him weary, and he refreshed himself there.

en.L: And the king and all the people who [were] with him came weary, and he refreshed himself there.
en.B: The king and all the people with him arrived worn out, and he rested there and recovered his strength.
en.R: The king and all the people with him were very tired when they reached the place where they stopped. There David rested and got his strength back.

es.L: Y el rey y todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él llegaron cansados, y allí se recobró.
es.B: El rey y toda la gente que estaba con él llegaron agotados, y allí descansó y recobró las fuerzas.
es.R: El rey y toda la gente que estaba con él llegaron muy cansados al lugar donde se detuvieron. Allí David descansó y recobró las fuerzas.

fr.L: Et le roi et tout le peuple qui [était] avec lui arrivèrent épuisés, et il reprit haleine là.
fr.B: Le roi et tout le peuple qui l’accompagnait arrivèrent épuisés, et là il se reposa et reprit des forces.
fr.R: Le roi et tout le peuple qui était avec lui étaient très fatigués quand ils sont arrivés à l’endroit où ils se sont arrêtés. Là, David s’est reposé et a repris des forces.

sw.L: Mfalme na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye wakafika wamechoka, naye akapumzika huko.
sw.B: Mfalme na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye wakafika wakiwa wamechoka sana, naye akapumzika huko akapata nguvu tena.
sw.R: Mfalme na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye walikuwa wamechoka sana walipofika mahali walipopumzika. Huko Daudi akapumzika na kupata nguvu tena.

vi.L: Vua và toàn dân theo vua đến nơi, mệt mỏi, và vua nghỉ lấy sức tại đó.
vi.B: Vua và toàn dân đi theo vua đến nơi thì đã kiệt sức, và vua nghỉ ngơi lấy lại sức tại đó.
vi.R: Khi đến chỗ dừng chân, vua và tất cả những người đi theo vua đều rất mệt. Tại đó Đa-vít nghỉ ngơi và lấy lại sức.

ko.L: 왕과 그와 함께 있던 모든 백성이 지쳐서 도착했고, 그는 거기에서 숨을 돌렸다.
ko.B: 왕과 그와 함께한 모든 백성은 지칠 대로 지쳐서 도착했다. 왕은 거기에서 쉬면서 기운을 되찾았다.
ko.R: 왕과 함께 있던 모든 백성은 쉴 곳에 이르렀을 때 몹시 지쳐 있었다. 다윗은 그곳에서 쉬면서 기운을 되찾았다.

decisions.choice: came weary ... there: the place they reached is not named
decisions.reason: "There" seems to point to a place, but the Hebrew names none. Some think "weary" (Ayephim) is itself the name of a stopping place, "they came to Ayephim". Some Greek manuscripts add "to the Jordan", where David is in 17:16-22. The text here keeps "weary", the plain sense of the word, and leaves the place unnamed.

decisions.choice: refreshed himself: caught his breath and recovered
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for breath and life. It is used of resting after hard labor (Exodus 23:12; 31:17).

decisions.choice: the place where they stopped; David
decisions.reason: Readable supplies what "there" refers to and names the king, keeping the place unnamed as the Hebrew does (m1).

source.text: וְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Absalom and all the people, [the] men of Israel, came [to] Jerusalem, and Ahithophel [was] with him.

en.L: Now Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came [to] Jerusalem, and Ahithophel [was] with him.
en.B: Meanwhile Absalom came to Jerusalem with all the people, the men of Israel, and Ahithophel was with him.
en.R: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the Israelites who followed him came into Jerusalem. Ahithophel came with him.

es.L: Y Absalón y todo el pueblo, los hombres de Israel, entraron [en] Jerusalén, y Ahitofel [estaba] con él.
es.B: Mientras tanto, Absalón entró en Jerusalén con todo el pueblo, los hombres de Israel, y Ahitofel estaba con él.
es.R: Mientras tanto, Absalón y todos los israelitas que lo seguían entraron en Jerusalén. Ahitofel iba con él.

fr.L: Or Absalom et tout le peuple, les hommes d’Israël, entrèrent [à] Jérusalem, et Ahitofel [était] avec lui.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, Absalom entra à Jérusalem avec tout le peuple, les hommes d’Israël, et Ahitofel était avec lui.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, Absalom et tous les Israélites qui le suivaient sont entrés dans Jérusalem. Ahitofel était venu avec lui.

sw.L: Basi Absalomu na watu wote, watu wa Israeli, wakaja Yerusalemu, na Ahithofeli [alikuwa] pamoja naye.
sw.B: Wakati huo Absalomu akaja Yerusalemu pamoja na watu wote, watu wa Israeli, na Ahithofeli alikuwa pamoja naye.
sw.R: Wakati huo, Absalomu na Waisraeli wote waliomfuata wakaingia Yerusalemu. Ahithofeli alikuja pamoja naye.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm và toàn dân, là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, và A-hi-tô-phe [ở] với chàng.
vi.B: Trong khi đó, Áp-sa-lôm cùng toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo vào Giê-ru-sa-lem, và A-hi-tô-phe cũng đi với chàng.
vi.R: Trong lúc đó, Áp-sa-lôm và tất cả những người Y-sơ-ra-ên theo chàng kéo vào Giê-ru-sa-lem. A-hi-tô-phe cũng đi với chàng.

ko.L: 한편 압살롬과 모든 백성, 곧 이스라엘 사람들이 예루살렘에 들어왔고, 아히도벨도 그와 함께 있었다.
ko.B: 그동안 압살롬은 모든 백성, 곧 이스라엘 사람들과 함께 예루살렘에 들어왔다. 아히도벨도 그와 함께 있었다.
ko.R: 그동안 압살롬과 그를 따르는 이스라엘 사람들이 모두 예루살렘에 들어왔다. 아히도벨도 압살롬과 함께 왔다.

decisions.choice: now Absalom: the scene turns back to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Putting Absalom's name first marks a change of scene to events at the same time. The story picks up from 15:37, where Hushai reached the city just as Absalom was entering it.

decisions.choice: all the people, the men of Israel: Absalom's supporters from the tribes
decisions.reason: "The men of Israel" explains "all the people": the Israelites whose hearts Absalom had won (15:6, 13), now marching with him as his force.

decisions.choice: Ahithophel: David's counselor who joined Absalom
decisions.reason: Ahithophel of Giloh had been David's adviser; he sided with Absalom at the start of the revolt (15:12, 31). His son Eliam was one of David's warriors (23:34), and Bathsheba's father was named Eliam (11:3), so he may have been her grandfather.

decisions.choice: all the Israelites who followed him
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two phrases and says that these Israelites were Absalom's followers (m2).

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֞א חוּשַׁ֧י הָאַרְכִּ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אֶל־אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חוּשַׁי֙ אֶל־אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יְחִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when came Hushai the Archite, [the] friend of David, to Absalom, and said Hushai to Absalom, may live the king! May live the king!

en.L: And when Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "May the king live! May the king live!"
en.B: When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to him, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
en.R: Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom. He said to him, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

es.L: Y cuando Husai el arquita, amigo de David, vino a Absalón, Husai dijo a Absalón: «¡Viva el rey! ¡Viva el rey!».
es.B: Cuando Husai el arquita, amigo de David, llegó adonde estaba Absalón, le dijo: «¡Viva el rey! ¡Viva el rey!».
es.R: Husai el arquita, el amigo de David, fue a ver a Absalón. Le dijo: «¡Viva el rey! ¡Viva el rey!».

fr.L: Et quand Houshaï l’Arkite, l’ami de David, vint auprès d’Absalom, Houshaï dit à Absalom : « Vive le roi ! Vive le roi ! »
fr.B: Quand Houshaï l’Arkite, l’ami de David, arriva auprès d’Absalom, il lui dit : « Vive le roi ! Vive le roi ! »
fr.R: Houshaï l’Arkite, l’ami de David, est venu voir Absalom. Il lui a dit : « Vive le roi ! Vive le roi ! »

sw.L: Ikawa Hushai Mwarki, rafiki wa Daudi, alipokuja kwa Absalomu, Hushai akamwambia Absalomu, "Mfalme na aishi! Mfalme na aishi!"
sw.B: Hushai Mwarki, rafiki wa Daudi, alipokuja kwa Absalomu, Hushai akamwambia, "Mfalme na aishi maisha marefu! Mfalme na aishi maisha marefu!"
sw.R: Hushai Mwarki, rafiki wa Daudi, akaja kwa Absalomu. Akamwambia, "Aishi maisha marefu mfalme! Aishi maisha marefu mfalme!"

vi.L: Khi Hu-sai người Ạt-kít, bạn của Đa-vít, đến gặp Áp-sa-lôm, Hu-sai nói với Áp-sa-lôm: "Vua vạn tuế! Vua vạn tuế!"
vi.B: Khi Hu-sai người Ạt-kít, bạn của Đa-vít, đến gặp Áp-sa-lôm, ông tung hô: "Vua vạn tuế! Vua vạn tuế!"
vi.R: Hu-sai người Ạt-kít, bạn của Đa-vít, đến gặp Áp-sa-lôm. Ông nói với chàng: "Vua vạn tuế! Vua vạn tuế!"

ko.L: 다윗의 친구 아렉 사람 후새가 압살롬에게 왔을 때, 후새가 압살롬에게 말했다. "왕께서 사시기를 빕니다! 왕께서 사시기를 빕니다!"
ko.B: 다윗의 친구인 아렉 사람 후새가 압살롬에게 나아가 말했다. "왕 만세! 왕 만세!"
ko.R: 다윗의 친구인 아렉 사람 후새가 압살롬에게 왔다. 후새가 압살롬에게 말했다. "왕 만세! 왕 만세!"

decisions.choice: the friend of David: a trusted adviser at court
decisions.reason: "The king's friend" was a position at court, the king's close confidant (15:37; 1 Kings 4:5; 1 Chronicles 27:33). David had sent Hushai back to Jerusalem to defeat Ahithophel's advice (15:32-37).

decisions.choice: the Archite: from the clan of Archi
decisions.reason: The Archites lived on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin, near Bethel (Joshua 16:2).

decisions.choice: May the king live: which king he means is left open
decisions.reason: The cry is the people's acclaim for a king (1 Samuel 10:24). Hushai does not say Absalom's name. Absalom hears himself hailed, but the reader, who knows why Hushai came (15:34), may hear it as meant for David.

decisions.choice: Long live the king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the usual English form of the cry, as in 1 Samuel 10:24; Literal keeps the Hebrew wish form.

decisions.choice: "Vua vạn tuế!"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese acclaim for a king; like the Hebrew, it does not name which king.

decisions.choice: "왕께서 사시기를 빕니다" (L); "왕 만세" (B, R), with "왕" rather than the address "임금님"
decisions.reason: Hushai does not say which king he means. Korean "임금님" would address Absalom directly; "왕" keeps the cry as open as the Hebrew.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־חוּשַׁ֔י זֶ֥ה חַסְדְּךָ֖ אֶת־רֵעֶ֑ךָ לָ֥מָּה לֹֽא־הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֶת־רֵעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Absalom to Hushai, [is] this your steadfast love with your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?

en.L: And Absalom said to Hushai, "[Is] this your steadfast love to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
en.B: Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your faithful love for your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
en.R: Absalom asked Hushai, "Is this how you show faithful love to your friend David? Why did you not go with him?"

es.L: Y Absalón dijo a Husai: «¿[Es] este tu amor leal para con tu amigo? ¿Por qué no fuiste con tu amigo?».
es.B: Absalón le dijo a Husai: «¿Es este tu amor fiel por tu amigo? ¿Por qué no te fuiste con tu amigo?».
es.R: Absalón le preguntó a Husai: «¿Así es como le muestras amor fiel a tu amigo David? ¿Por qué no te fuiste con él?».

fr.L: Et Absalom dit à Houshaï : « [Est-ce] là ton amour loyal envers ton ami ? Pourquoi n’es-tu pas allé avec ton ami ? »
fr.B: Absalom dit à Houshaï : « Est-ce là ton amour fidèle pour ton ami ? Pourquoi n’es-tu pas parti avec ton ami ? »
fr.R: Absalom a demandé à Houshaï : « C’est comme ça que tu montres ton amour fidèle à ton ami David ? Pourquoi n’es-tu pas parti avec lui ? »

sw.L: Absalomu akamwambia Hushai, "Je, huu [ndio] upendo wako usiokoma kwa rafiki yako? Kwa nini hukwenda pamoja na rafiki yako?"
sw.B: Absalomu akamwambia Hushai, "Je, hizi ndizo fadhili zako kwa rafiki yako? Kwa nini hukwenda pamoja na rafiki yako?"
sw.R: Absalomu akamwuliza Hushai, "Je, hivi ndivyo unavyomwonyesha rafiki yako Daudi fadhili? Kwa nini hukwenda pamoja naye?"

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm nói với Hu-sai: "Đây [là] tình yêu thương thành tín của ông đối với bạn ông sao? Sao ông không đi với bạn ông?"
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm hỏi Hu-sai: "Đây là lòng nhân từ của ông đối với bạn mình sao? Sao ông không đi theo bạn ông?"
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm hỏi Hu-sai: "Ông tỏ lòng nhân từ với bạn ông là Đa-vít như thế này sao? Sao ông không đi với ông ấy?"

ko.L: 압살롬이 후새에게 말했다. "이것이 네 친구에게 [베푸는] 네 한결같은 사랑이냐? 어찌하여 네 친구와 함께 가지 않았느냐?"
ko.B: 압살롬이 후새에게 말했다. "이것이 네 친구에 대한 네 인애냐? 왜 네 친구와 함께 가지 않았느냐?"
ko.R: 압살롬이 후새에게 물었다. "네 친구 다윗에게 인애를 베푼다는 것이 고작 이것이냐? 왜 그와 함께 가지 않았느냐?"

decisions.choice: steadfast love: the loyalty owed within a bond of friendship
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the faithful love that keeps a commitment, here between David and his friend (as between David and Jonathan, 1 Samuel 20:8, 14-15). Absalom asks why Hushai has broken it.

decisions.choice: is this ...? why ...?: a test of Hushai's loyalty
decisions.reason: Absalom's questions are sharp and mocking. He uses Hushai's own title, "friend", against him, to see whether he can be trusted.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (L); faithful love (B, R)
decisions.reason: As set for these books, chesed is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: your friend David
decisions.reason: Readable names the friend.

decisions.choice: Absalom, now king, says "ông" to the older Hushai; Hushai says "vua" / "bệ hạ" / "đức vua" and "tôi"
decisions.reason: Absalom courts David's old friend; he mocks him, but still speaks to an elder politely.

decisions.choice: Absalom speaks to Hushai and to Ahithophel in the plain style (해라체); they answer him in the formal style (합쇼체) and call him "임금님"
alternatives: the polite style toward older counselors
decisions.reason: Absalom now acts as king, and his counselors address him as king; the plain style matches David's own speech to his officials.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־אַבְשָׁלֹם֒ לֹ֕א כִּי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ל֥וֹ אֶהְיֶ֖ה וְאִתּ֥וֹ אֵשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Hushai to Absalom, no, for [the one] whom has chosen Yahweh and this people and every man of Israel, to him I will be, and with him I will remain.

en.L: And Hushai said to Absalom, "No, for the one whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will remain.
